slides.texte_overlay: Learn three names in every new group. Use them in the first five minutes. Remembering names makes people warm up to you right away.
Talk to the people you see every day. The barista, your neighbour, the gym regular. Small daily chats build social confidence without pressure.
Have a go-to question. "What's keeping you busy these days?" It works with anyone and opens much better conversations than "what do you do?"
Leave conversations on a high. Don't wait for the awkward silence. End while it's fun and people will want to talk to you again. Try it this week.
Before: I avoided parties because I didn't know what to say. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have stories.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I avoided parties because I didn't know what to say. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have stories.

slides.texte_overlay: Follow up after you meet someone. "Great talking yesterday, let's grab a coffee." Most people never do, so it makes you stand out.
Join a team or a club. Football, chess, climbing. A shared activity gives you a group of friends without having to start from scratch.
